commit_message:
[HAL] Memoize allocator selects in program order (#25243)

MemoizeDeviceSelection processed its select groups in DenseMap order,
which follows attribute addresses, so the names of the generated globals
(`__allocator_select_device` vs `_device_0`, etc) changed between runs
and `.vmfb` files of multi-device modules were not reproducible. This
does not affect correctness, only the reproducibility of `.vmfb` files.

The fix uses a MapVector to process the groups in the order of their
first select.

The lit test now checks exact names instead of capturing them with `.*`
to avoid matching only the prefix part of the name.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: Zmicier Prybysh <zprybysh@baylibre.com>

commit_message:
[CI] Use the Azure sccache in the BYO LLVM build

linux_x64_clang_byollvm still reads the GCS ccache. Nothing has written
to that cache since https://github.com/iree-org/iree/pull/18511 moved
the Linux jobs to the Azure sccache, so every run builds LLVM, MLIR and
IREE from scratch. The scheduled runs take 3 to 5 hours and sometimes
hit the 6-hour job timeout.

Use the Azure sccache with its own key prefix, like the other jobs on
the cpubuilder_ubuntu_jammy image. byo_llvm.sh always passed ccache as
the compiler launcher. It now uses the launcher from the environment if
one is set. LLVM turns off precompiled headers when the launcher is
sccache.

Without the secret, for example in pull requests from forks,
setup_sccache.sh leaves sccache off and the job uses ccache as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Tobias Fuchs <fuchs@roofline.ai>
